title: GameLoop Android Media Process Has Stopped: Safe Crash Fixes
summary: Troubleshoot GameLoop media-process errors and PUBG Mobile crashes without deleting unrelated Windows files.
intro: The Android error stating that a media process has stopped can appear after an emulator update, a game reinstall or corrupted local app data. It does not, on its own, prove that the GPU is defective or the account has been banned. This guide works from reversible checks toward more disruptive repair steps, with an emphasis on retaining user data and avoiding unsafe third-party cleanup scripts.

sections.heading: Capture the actual failure
paragraphs: Write down the full error message and when it appears: on launcher startup, during PUBG loading or several minutes into a match. Note whether Windows reports an application crash at the same time. A screenshot and Windows Reliability Monitor entry are more useful than a generic claim that GameLoop is broken. Record the emulator and game versions before performing any repair so a later recurrence can be traced.

sections.heading: Restart and check available storage
paragraphs: Close all GameLoop components normally, then restart Windows to clear stale processes and file locks. Verify that the system drive and emulator installation drive have comfortable free space for downloads and temporary data. If an update was interrupted, launch the supported updater and let it finish. Avoid deleting random Android system folders because seemingly disposable files can contain necessary package metadata or account settings.

sections.heading: Separate app cache from app data
paragraphs: A launcher may expose an official repair or cache-clearing feature; prefer that over manually removing unknown directories. Cache removal is different from wiping Android application data, which may remove downloads, login state and local settings. Verify that your game account is securely linked before considering any reset. Export important key mappings or screenshots where supported so they can be restored after a clean reinstall.

sections.heading: Check security and driver conflicts
paragraphs: Review Windows Security history for quarantined emulator components and check whether multiple antivirus products are interfering. Only restore files you can verify came from the official vendor. Update GPU drivers through supported sources and test without unnecessary overlays. Do not permanently disable Windows protections or add a broad folder exclusion merely to suppress an error; doing so weakens protection without proving the underlying issue.

sections.heading: Reinstall only after basic repair fails
paragraphs: If official repair and updates do not help, uninstall GameLoop using its supported uninstaller. Back up user-created configuration first, then remove residual folders only when their ownership is confirmed. A one-click script that recursively deletes everything containing a vague emulator keyword can destroy unrelated applications. Reinstall from the official source, update the engine and verify a clean launch before restoring custom settings.

sections.heading: Diagnose after recovery
paragraphs: Run a short match using default graphics and key mapping, then increase settings gradually. If the error returns after a specific renderer or resolution change, that is a useful clue. Keep logs private because they may contain account identifiers or local paths. Escalate persistent crashes with a concise report to official support instead of experimenting with anti-cheat bypasses or modified game packages.
